{"title":"JOINT INTEGRATED PRIORITIZED TARGET LIST (JIPTL) - INDOPACOM SHIELD MDIX ATO Cycle 01","docType":"JIPTL","content":"UNCLASSIFIED // FOR OFFICIAL USE ONLY

JOINT INTEGRATED PRIORITIZED TARGET LIST (JIPTL)
Operation: INDOPACOM SHIELD — Western Pacific Multi-Domain Integration Exercise (MDIX)
ATO Cycle: MDIX ATO Cycle 01
Effective Dates: 01 MAR 2026 0001Z — 08 MAR 2026 2400Z
Classification: UNCLASSIFIED // FOUO
Issuing Authority: J-5 Plans & Policy, United States Indo-Pacific Command (USINDOPACOM)

PURPOSE: This JIPTL provides a prioritized, theater-level list of simulated target sets for the MDIX exercise window (01–08 MAR 2026). Targets and effects are constructed to validate joint multi-domain integration under conditions of contested logistics, degraded/intermittent space-enabled services, and contested information environments. All target names, locations, and identifiers herein are fictionalized and sanitized for exercise use and are not intended to direct real-world operations. This JIPTL is traceable to higher-level strategic priorities in the NDS Extract, NMS Theater Annex, and JSCP tasking for DENY, DEGRADE, PROTECT, SUSTAIN, and DESTROY.

NOTE ON SCOPE AND SANITIZATION: In accordance with safety and legal constraints, this JIPTL intentionally omits actionable tactical procedures, weapons effects, unit-specific attack procedures, precise geospatial coordinates, radio frequencies, and targeting tactics. It provides higher-level target set descriptions, prioritized effects, and coordination requirements to enable realistic joint planning and execution within the exercise control framework.

PRIORITY 1
Effect: DENY / DESTROY (Primary strategic aim: Prevent adversary immediate power projection and large-scale anti-access/area denial (A2/AD) capability employment)

Target Set: Theater Anti-Access/Area Denial Complex (A2/AD Node Cluster)
- BE Numbers: 0101 - 0110
  - BE 0101: "Coastal Integrated Air Defense Node Alpha" — Fixed integrated air defense sensor and engagement node (fictional). Location: Western Pacific coastal sector, exercise-designated grid NET-ALPHA-1.
  - BE 0102: "Long-Range Missile Forward Emplacement Bravo" — Hardened launch support and associated fuel/munitions storage (fictional). Location: NET-BRAVO-3.
  - BE 0103: "Maritime Strike Surface-to-Surface Relay Charlie" — Mobile SSM targeting and C2 relay (fictional). Location: NET-CHARLIE-2.
  - BE 0104: "Maritime Mines Depot Delta" — Coastal mine storage and deployment facilities (fictional). Location: NET-DELTA-4.
  - BE 0105: "Maritime Surveillance Over-The-Horizon Radar Echo" — Fixed OTH radar array (fictional). Location: NET-ECHO-1.
  - BE 0106: "Anti-Ship Cruise Missile Coastal Battery Foxtrot" — Coastal launch battery (fictional). Location: NET-FOXTROT-5.
  - BE 0107: "A2/AD C2 Node Gulf" — Theater-level C2 hub supporting A2/AD sensor-to-shooter links (fictional). Location: NET-GULF-1.
  - BE 0108: "Forward Electronic Warfare/ jamming Complex Hotel" — EW emitters supporting A2/AD operations (fictional). Location: NET-HOTEL-2.
  - BE 0109: "A2/AD Logistic Support Hub India" — Port/logistics node supporting A2/AD sustainment (fictional). Location: NET-INDIA-4.
  - BE 0110: "Sustainment Airfield Juliet" — Expeditionary airfield used to support long-range strike and rotary wing sorties (fictional). Location: NET-JULIET-3.

Justification: These target sets directly enable adversary denial of allied access and freedom of maneuver in the Western Pacific. Neutralizing or degrading these elements supports JSCP and NMS priorities to preserve US/partner freedom to maneuver, secure lines of communication, and enable follow-on joint operations. Action against these nodes removes or degrades hostile sensors, shooters, and sustainment chains that present immediate risk to friendly distributed forces.

COORDINATION:
- Joint Air and Maritime Components to coordinate deconfliction and phasing of neutralization effects through the Joint Air Tasking Order (exercise ATO) and maritime maneuver plans.
- Information Operations (IO)/Public Affairs (PA) cells to synchronize messaging with allied partners to manage escalation signaling as per NMS Theater Annex guidance.
- Logistics and Host Nation Liaison to pre-coordinate alternate port and airfield access for sustainment following simulated effects on adversary logistics hubs.
- Space/Cyber cells: prioritize resilient CIO and alternative communications methodologies; simulated degradation of adversary space-enabled ISR to be synchronized with friendly measures of contested communications.

PRIORITY 2
Effect: DEGRADE / DENY (Primary strategic aim: Impair adversary theater-level ISR, targeting, and precision strike networks to reduce enemy situational awareness and precision engagement capability)

Target Set: Theater Intelligence, Surveillance, Reconnaissance (ISR) and Targeting Network
- BE Numbers: 0201 - 0210
  - BE 0201: "Signals Intelligence Ground Processing Node Kilo" — Ground SIGINT processing and dissemination center (fictional). Location: NET-KILO-2.
  - BE 0202: "Maritime ISR Patrol Coordination Site Lima" — Coordination node for maritime UAV and manned patrols (fictional). Location: NET-LIMA-3.
  - BE 0203: "Tactical ISR Satellite Ground Station Mike" — Ground terminal supporting adversary space-based ISR (fictional). Location: NET-MIKE-1.
  - BE 0204: "Real-Time Targeting Fusion Cell November" — Theater-level targeting fusion and cueing cell (fictional). Location: NET-NOVEMBER-2.
  - BE 0205: "Persistent UAV Launch and Recovery Site Oscar" — Forward UAV basing and recovery (fictional). Location: NET-OSCAR-4.
  - BE 0206: "Maritime Acoustic Surveillance Array Papa" — Undersea sensor processing node (fictional). Location: NET-PAPA-5.
  - BE 0207: "Coastal Electro-Optical Sensor Grid Quebec" — EO/IR sensor clusters and data links (fictional). Location: NET-QUEBEC-2.
  - BE 0208: "Targeting Data Link Relay Romeo" — Communications relay node enabling real-time targeting (fictional). Location: NET-ROMEO-3.
  - BE 0209: "Meteorological and Oceanographic Support Site Sierra" — Environmental data node supporting weapons employment and ISR (fictional). Location: NET-SIERRA-1.
  - BE 0210: "Unmanned Systems Maintenance Depot Tango" — Depot for ISR systems sustainment (fictional). Location: NET-TANGO-4.

Justification: Degrading ISR and targeting nodes reduces adversary's ability to locate and prosecute friendly forces and protects distributed U.S. and partner assets. Prioritized in accordance with NDS priority PROTECT and NMS objective to preserve friendly C2 and survivability under degraded space services.

COORDINATION:
- J-2 (Intelligence) to validate simulated effects and collateral sensitivity; enforce classification and release limitations of ISR datasets within exercise.
- Cyber and Space Cells to model simulated interference with adversary data links and terminals; ensure exercise-controlled injection of degraded space services.
- Allied/partner ISR liaisons to coordinate simulated handover of search and track responsibilities in affected areas.
- Legal and Targeting working groups to review all simulated strike and non-kinetic options for compliance with exercise safety constraints.

PRIORITY 3
Effect: PROTECT / SUSTAIN (Primary strategic aim: Harden and preserve friendly sustainment lines, ports, logistics nodes, and distributed basing under contested logistics conditions)

Target Set: Friendly and Partner Sustainment Nodes (Force Protection & Resilient Logistics Emphasis)
- BE Numbers: 0301 - 0310
  - BE 0301: "Forward Sustainment Port Alpha (Friendly)" — Exercise-designated allied port used to receive sustainment shipments (fictional). Location: NET-PF-ALPHA.
  - BE 0302: "Distributed Expeditionary Airfield Bravo (Friendly)" — Small expeditionary airstrip for sustainment sorties (fictional). Location: NET-AF-BRAVO.
  - BE 0303: "Mobile Logistics Staging Area Charlie (Friendly)" — Inland staging node for joint sustainment (fictional). Location: NET-MLS-CHARLIE.
  - BE 0304: "Maritime Sustainment Connector Delta (Friendly)" — Pre-positioned afloat logistics element (fictional). Location: NET-MSC-DELTA.
  - BE 0305: "Fuel & Munitions Distribution Node Echo (Friendly)" — Bulk fuel and munitions receipt and distribution node (fictional). Location: NET-FMD-ECHO.
  - BE 0306: "Maintenance and Recovery Hub Foxtrot (Friendly)" — Repair hub enabling sortie generation (fictional). Location: NET-MRH-FOXTROT.
  - BE 0307: "Alternative Logistics Route Golf" — Secondary over-the-horizon resupply route (fictional). Location: NET-ALT-GOLF.
  - BE 0308: "Medical Evacuation and Treatment Site Hotel (Friendly)" — Theater medical hub (fictional). Location: NET-MED-HOTEL.
  - BE 0309: "Cyber-Resilient Logistics AIS Node India (Friendly)" — Information system supporting logistics visibility (fictional). Location: NET-CRL-INDIA.
  - BE 0310: "Partner Nation Host-Nation Support Coordination Cell Juliet" — Liaison and coordination center (fictional). Location: NET-HNS-JULIET.

Justification: Protecting and sustaining friendly nodes under contested logistics is critical to operational endurance and aligns to NDS line of effort SUSTAIN. Prioritization ensures redundancy, rapid restoration of supply chains, and continuity of joint operations under simulated interdiction.

COORDINATION:
- J-4 (Logistics) to manage exercise injects related to supply depletion, alternate routing, and host-nation coordination; maintain ship-to-shore and air delivery synchronization.
- Medical and Personnel Recovery representatives to manage simulated casualty flows and MEDEVAC routing under degraded comms.
- Host Nation/Regional Security Cooperation Staff to simulate diplomatic clearances for alternate basing as required by sustainment continuity.
- Contracting/Transportation nodes to execute simulated surge procurement and movement control measures.

PRIORITY 4
Effect: DEGRADE / DENY (Primary strategic aim: Disrupt adversary cyber, space, and EW capabilities that enable precision fires, C2, and A2/AD networks)

Target Set: Cyber, Electronic Warfare (EW), and Space Enablers
- BE Numbers: 0401 - 0408
  - BE 0401: "Theater Cyber Operations Coordination Node Kappa" — Cyber operations planning and command node (fictional). Location: NET-KAPPA-1.
  - BE 0402: "Electronic Warfare Forward Emission Cluster Lambda" — EW emitters supporting electronic surveillance and jamming (fictional). Location: NET-LAMBDA-2.
  - BE 0403: "Space Relay Terminal Mu" — Ground terminal facilitating adversary SATCOM relay (fictional). Location: NET-MU-1.
  - BE 0404: "Command & Control Data Center Nu" — Data center supporting theater C2 and targeting feeds (fictional). Location: NET-NU-3.
  - BE 0405: "Tactical Communications Node Xi" — Mobile communications node providing distal C2 connectivity (fictional). Location: NET-XI-4.
  - BE 0406: "Precision Navigation Augmentation Site Omicron" — Localized PNT augmentation node (fictional). Location: NET-OMICRON-2.
  - BE 0407: "Radio Relay and High-Frequency Broadcast Site Pi" — Broadcast facility for regional reach (fictional). Location: NET-PI-5.
  - BE 0408: "Maintenance Depot for Space & Cyber Assets Rho" — Maintenance and spare parts facility (fictional). Location: NET-RHO-3.

Justification: Disrupting cyber, EW, and space enablers contests the adversary’s ability to produce coordinated effects, consistent with NMS objectives to protect U.S. freedom of action in degraded space and contested EMS environments. Prioritization favors nodes that most directly enable targeting against friendly distributed forces.

COORDINATION:
- J-6 and USSF liaison to choreograph simulated space-denial and contested-signal events; ensure redundancy and alternative comms are tested.
- Cyber Command coordination cell to adjudicate simulated cyber operations injection and coordinate with allied cyber partners.
- IO and EW planners to sequence non-kinetic effects with kinetic/physical actions to validate integrated targeting and escalation management.
- Joint Targeting Board to adjudicate classification, law-of-war considerations, and collateral risk for simulated effects against dual-use infrastructure.

PRIORITY 5
Effect: DESTROY / DEGRADE (Primary strategic aim: Disrupt adversary sustainment lines of operation supporting regional mobilization and escalation capability)

Target Set: Strategic Logistics and Mobilization Nodes (Adversary)
- BE Numbers: 0501 - 0510
  - BE 0501: "Rail and Road Junction Mobilization Hub Sigma" — Key intermodal transfer point for force mobilization (fictional). Location: NET-SIGMA-4.
  - BE 0502: "Maritime Roll-On/Roll-Off (RoRo) Assembly Site Tau" — Vehicle and equipment assembly and embarkation yard (fictional). Location: NET-TAU-2.
  - BE 0503: "Ammunition and War Reserve Depot Upsilon" — Bulk ammunition storage and distribution (fictional). Location: NET-UPLON-1.
  - BE 0504: "Forward Repair and Sustainment Yard Phi" — Repair yard for maritime and land equipment (fictional). Location: NET-PHI-3.
  - BE 0505: "Mobilization Airlift Staging Area Chi" — Staging area for airlifted materiel and personnel (fictional). Location: NET-CHI-2.
  - BE 0506: "Civil Infrastructure Logistics Node Psi" — Civil port and associated civil-military logistics interfaces (fictional). Location: NET-PSI-5.
  - BE 0507: "Strategic Fuel Pipeline and Storage Omega" — Bulk petroleum distribution node (fictional). Location: NET-OMEGA-1.
  - BE 0508: "Strategic Communications Backbone Node Alpha-2" — Backbone node supporting national and theater mobilization communications (fictional). Location: NET-BB-A2.
  - BE 0509: "Expeditionary Sealift Staging Area Beta-2" — Staging area for sealift prepositioning (fictional). Location: NET-ES-B2.
  - BE 0510: "Dual-Use Commercial Logistics Consolidation Center Gamma-2" — Commercial consolidation center used for rapid mobilization (fictional). Location: NET-CLC-G2.

Justification: Degrading adversary mobilization and sustainment nodes reduces their capacity to escalate and rapidly project forces. This supports the NDS goals of integrated deterrence and constraining adversary escalation options while protecting regional stability.

COORDINATION:
- Interagency and diplomatic channels to model international economic and commercial impacts of simulated actions against dual-use nodes.
- Host-nation engagement and legal advisors to craft messaging and exercise control environments preventing real-world misinterpretation.
- Combined Logistics and Transportation Working Group to validate alternate supply pathways and exercise commercial-military coordination in the simulation.
- Environmental and civil-military coordination cells to manage simulated collateral impacts in exercise control scenarios.

TARGETING TEMPO, CONTROL, AND SAFETY
- Execution of simulated effects will be phased through the MDIX ATO cycle and daily targeting synchronization boards under J-3 control. All actions will respect exercise safety, legal review, and escalation control measures prescribed by USINDOPACOM.
- Simulated effects will be adjudicated through the Joint Targeting Board (JTB) and disseminated in sanitized ATO Annexes for component execution. All component requests for additional prioritization adjustments must be submitted to USINDOPACOM J-5/J-3 via established exercise coordination channels.
- Collateral Risk Mitigation: All proposed simulated actions against dual-use or populated nodes will be subjected to enhanced collateral effects review; in simulation, non-kinetic options will be prioritized where feasible to achieve desired effect while minimizing simulated physical harm.

LINKAGE TO STRATEGIC PRIORITIES
- DENY / DESTROY (Priority 1, Priority 5): Targets that remove immediate A2/AD and mobilization capability align to NDS objective to deny adversary power projection and constrain escalation.
- DEGRADE / DENY (Priority 2, Priority 4): Disrupting ISR, cyber, EW, and space enablers supports theater-level information advantage and protects friendly C2 under degraded space conditions per NMS annex.
- PROTECT / SUSTAIN (Priority 3): Hardened friendly sustainment nodes ensure operational endurance and align to JSCP emphasis on contested logistics readiness.

AUTHORITY AND REVIEW
- This JIPTL is issued for MDIX exercise purposes only and derived from JSCP/CONPLAN/OPLAN authorities dated 01 MAR 2026. All items are subject to daily review and re-prioritization by the J-5/J-3 targeting cell in coordination with component targeting leads, the JTB, and legal advisors.
- Changes to priority or effect require concurrence of the J-5 (Plans & Policy) and J-3 (Operations) exercising authority.

RESTRICTIONS
- No real-world coordinates, targeting firing solutions, unit-level strike procedures, radio frequencies, or specific weapon employment guidance are included in this document.
- Any reference to “nodes,” “depots,” or “sites” is fictionalized for exercise realism and must not be applied to real-world targeting processes.

ANNEX: Exercise Coordination Checklist (summary)
- Daily Targeting Synchronization Meeting time and location to be promulgated via exercise orders.
- Component targeting leads to provide simulated battle damage assessment (BDA) inputs within 6 hours of simulated action completion.
- IO/PA to approve all public statements and internal messaging templates prior to release.
- Civil-Military Coordination cell to manage simulated humanitarian and infrastructure impacts and provide recommended mitigations.

Date/Time Prepared: 28 FEB 2026 1400Z
Distribution: USINDOPACOM Components, Joint Staff (J-3/J-5/J-2/J-4/J-6), Service Component Targeting Cells, Allied/Partner Exercise Liaisons

{
  "title": "SPECIAL INSTRUCTIONS (SPINS) — INDOPACOM Western Pacific MDIX",
  "docType": "SPINS",
  "content": "UNCLASSIFIED // FOUO
SPECIAL INSTRUCTIONS (SPINS)
INDOPACOM — WESTERN PACIFIC
MULTI-DOMAIN INTEGRATION EXERCISE (MDIX) / OPERATION INDOPACOM SHIELD
EFFECTIVE: 01–08 MAR 2026

PURPOSE: These Special Instructions (SPINS) provide standardized, theater-level operating procedures, restrictions, frequencies, and deconfliction measures to enable safe, coordinated, and resilient multi-domain operations in the Western Pacific MDIX window. All units, components, and combined/partner forces participating in MDIX shall comply with these SPINS. These instructions implement and are traceable to the NDS Extract (01 MAR 2026), NMS Theater Annex (01 MAR 2026), JSCP tasking (01 MAR 2026), and INDOPACOM CONPLAN/OPLAN (Operation INDOPACOM SHIELD). This document is UNCLASSIFIED // FOUO.

CONTENTS:
1. GENERAL (ROE, PID, CIVCAS AVERSION)
2. AIRSPACE CONTROL (ALTITUDE DECONFLICTION, RESTRICTED/CONTROLLED AREAS, ROZ/COORDINATES)
3. TANKER OPERATIONS (AIR REFUELING TRACKS, AIRCRAFT, FUEL STATES, RECOVERY PROCEDURES)
4. CSAR (ALERT POSTURE, TASKED UNITS, FREQUENCIES, RECOVERY PROCEDURES)
5. SPACE SUPPORT (GPS DEGRADATION WARNINGS, SATCOM PRIORITY, OPIR/SSA DATA FEEDS)
6. COMMUNICATIONS (PRIMARY/BACKUP FREQUENCIES, NET STRUCTURE, EMCON/ANTI-JAM PROCEDURES)

1. GENERAL
1.1 Applicability. These SPINS apply to all US forces, assigned/attached allied and partner forces, and contracted aviation participating in MDIX in the INDOPACOM Western Pacific AOR 01–08 MAR 2026. Compliance with these SPINS is mandatory; deviations must be coordinated with the applicable component Airspace Control Authority (ACA)/Joint Force Air Component (JFAC) and approved by CDRUSINDOPACOM staff J5/J3.

1.2 Rules of Engagement (ROE) & Use of Force.
  a. ROE governing MDIX are issued separately (ROE Annex A) and remain in effect. Except where explicit exercise injects alter, the baseline ROE are conservative and emphasize de-escalation consistent with the NDS Extract priorities: DENY coercive advantage, PROTECT forces and partners, and PREVENT unintended escalation.
  b. Positive Identification (PID) requirement. Positive Identification shall be established prior to the use of lethal force against any air or maritime contact unless hostile intent or hostile act is unambiguously evident. PID standards: visual ID, IFF Mode 4/5/Enhanced Mode 5 authentication, EW signature correlation, or validated intelligence cue. Units must document PID process and time-stamp evidence in mission reports.
  c. Escalation control. All engagements that could produce kinetic effects beyond self-defense require immediate report to JFC (via JOC/J3) and clearance per the escalation matrix in the ROE Annex.

1.3 Civilian Casualty Avoidance (CIVCAS).
  a. Risk Mitigation. Units will apply the law of armed conflict (LOAC) principles of distinction, proportionality, and precaution. Targeting and weapons employment must consider population centers, port/harbor infrastructure, and commercial shipping lanes.
  b. Civilian objects. Ports, commercial airfields, major industrial complexes, offshore windfarms, undersea telecommunications infrastructure, and humanitarian assistance staging areas are designated protected or restricted for MDIX unless specifically released in writing by the JFC. Any planned fires, blasts, or emissions that could affect civilian mariner/air traffic require 72-hour NOTAM/NOTMAR coordination unless waived by CDRUSINDOPACOM J3.
  c. Pre- and post-strike measures. Information operations must include warnings to minimize CIVCAS where feasible. Immediate post-event battle damage assessments (BDA) shall include CIVCAS estimates and be forwarded to the JOC and HN liaison elements.

1.4 Identification, Friend or Foe (IFF).
  a. All participating aircraft will operate IFF Mode 5 and S-TTL authentication where equipment permits. Non-compliant aircraft will be restricted to corridors and require flight-following by a designated control agency.
  b. Maritime forces will operate designated AIS profiles consistent with operational security (OPSEC) guidance; AIS may be selectively withheld during deniable or contested phases—such withholding must be coordinated through the maritime component.

2. AIRSPACE CONTROL
2.1 Airspace Control System. The INDOPACOM ACA establishes an Airspace Control Order (ACO) daily. The ACO governs controlled, restricted, and advisory airspace for MDIX. The Joint Airspace Management Cell (JAMC) will publish ACO updates at H-12 and H-2 daily during MDIX; emergency updates may be released as required.

2.2 Altitude Deconfliction.
  a. All participating fixed- and rotary-wing aircraft will adhere to the altitude strata in the ACO unless specifically cleared otherwise:
     - LOW STRATA (Surface to FL150): Assigned to maritime helicopters, littoral strike craft, tactical lift (CH-53, MH-60, V-22), and some UAV BLOS denied operations.
     - MID STRATA (FL150 to FL260): Assigned to tactical fighters (F-35A/B/C, F-22), CAS, and some ISR/ELINT platforms.
     - HIGH STRATA (FL260 and above): Assigned to strategic lift, AEW (E-2D, E-3/Future), high-altitude ISR, and air-refueling tankers when operating at altitude.
  b. Vertical buffer zones. A 1,000 ft buffer above/below assigned altitude layers will be enforced for all non-emergency transit. Emergency maneuvers must be annunciated on the appropriate airspace net immediately.

2.3 Restriction/Operating Zones (ROZ) & Coordinates.
  a. All ROZ/No-Fly/Control Areas listed below are exercise specific and in effect for MDIX. Coordinates in WGS-84 (Lat/Long, decimal degrees). Times are ZULU.
     - ROZ-01 (Archipelago East Corridor): 18.5000N 144.8000E to 18.9000N 145.6000E — radius 35 NM sector; alt: SFC–FL150; active 01–08 MAR 2026 0000–2359Z. Reserved for rotary-wing CSAR and partner maritime insertion training. All overflights require ACA clearance.
     - ROZ-02 (Central Exercise Area - North): 20.2500N 150.5000E center, radius 50 NM; alt: SFC–FL260; active 02–06 MAR 0600–1800Z. Reserved for combined strike package integration; dynamic deconfliction required.
     - ROZ-03 (Central Exercise Area - South): 18.0000N 148.0000E center, radius 40 NM; alt: SFC–FL360; active 03–05 MAR 0200–2200Z. Reserved for high-altitude ISR and tanking corridors.
     - ROZ-04 (Critical Sea Line of Communication (SLOC) Cover): 16.2000N 147.5000E to 17.8000N 149.1000E box; alt: SFC–Unlimited; active 01–08 MAR 0000–2359Z; maritime and air anti-access/area denial (A2/AD) suppression demonstration area. Commercial shipping advised to transit outside or with prior coordination.
  b. Restricted Operating Zones (dynamic). Temporary ROZs (T-ROZ) will be published via ACO and broadcast on the Airspace Management Net when live fires, EW emissions, or live ship-surface gunfire are underway. T-ROZ coordinates and times will be promulgated minimum 30 minutes prior to activation, except for safety/case-of-force incidents.

2.4 Airspace Reserved for Partner/Allied Forces. Allied national air elements (e.g., PACAF-liaison collection) will be allocated corridors and altitudes per the ACO. National caveats must be honored; component ACA will annotate in daily ATO/ACO.

2.5 Deconfliction Procedures. Mission planners must coordinate via the JAMC and submit intent messages (MISSION INTENT) at H-24 and H-3. Real-time deconfliction via the Airspace Management Net is required before entering an active ROZ.

3. TANKER OPERATIONS (AIR REFUELING)
3.1 Air Refueling Tracks (AR Tracks).
  a. Primary AR Track A1 (North Track) — Center 20.8000N 151.2000E; track length 150 NM (west-east); operating altitude FL260–FL300; bearings 090/270 true. Assigned to KC-135R/RT/SG and KC-46A AR platforms. Active 01–08 MAR 0400–2200Z daily for fighter/tactical sorties.
  b. Secondary AR Track S1 (South Track) — Center 18.5000N 148.5000E; track length 120 NM (NW-SE); alt FL220–FL260; bearings 135/315 true. Assigned to KC-46A and allied tanker detachments. Active 02–07 MAR 0200–2000Z.
  c. Contingency AR Holding Tracks (CHT) — allocated adjacent to ROZ-03 to enable rapid rejoin for CAP and high-altitude ISR (CHT-1 Center 19.2000N 149.0000E radius 30 NM).

3.2 Tanker Units and On-Station Procedures.
  a. Designated tanker units: 22 ARW (KC-135R), 6 ARW (KC-46A), and rotational tankers from theater-based detachments (E.g., 36 ARW). Allied tankers (e.g., RAAF KC-30A) may be integrated per SOFA/MDIX LOA.
  b. Tanker on-station fuel state (minimums). Tankers will declare minimum recovery fuel states per component Air Refueling SOP: bingo state to home base—contingent on mission; scheduled bingo for receiver planning: 8,500 lbs (KC-135), 12,000 lbs (KC-46A). Emergency fuel states must be broadcast on the Air Refueling Net and visible to receiver via pre-briefed callsigns.
  c. Aircrew Procedures. Standard ASTP or case I/II/III AR procedures per the Air Refueling Handbook apply. All receivers and tankers shall brief HOOK/RELEASE contingency procedures for ECM/jamming events.

3.3 Air Refueling Frequencies & Callsigns.
  a. Air Refueling Net (Primary): UHF LOS — 301.725 MHz AM (designated AES: ARNET-INDO-PAC A). Backup: 135.975 MHz AM.
  b. Tanker Control Callsigns: "STARLIFT-AR" (KC-135/46 organic to 5/7 AFCENT-like tasking), "BLUEARROW" (allied tankers), "JACKAL-AR" (theater rapid response).
  c. Emergency jettison/kill switch procedures. All tankers will conform to wing-specific emergency procedures; jettison of fuel only authorized when necessary to prevent flight safety hazard; coordinate with ACA and JOC.

4. CSAR (Combat Search and Rescue)
4.1 CSAR Alert Posture. CSAR posture will be maintained at two levels:
  - ALERT I (Cover/Immediate Response): 1 HH-60G (Air Force) + 1 AH-64 (escort) within 30 minutes flying time from Primary Rescue Base (PRB) — PRB coordinates: 20.1500N 149.8500E (US Navy forward base). Active availability 24/7 MDIX.
  - ALERT II (Area Response): 2 USMC CH-53E or MV-22s at alternate recovery sites within 90 minutes flying time. Prepositioning by CH-53E/HC-130 crews near ROZ-01 during high-density strike operations.

4.2 Tasked Units.
  a. USAF CSAR: 38th Rescue Squadron (HH-60G/HC-130J) task-organized under the Theater Rescue Coordination Center (TRCC).
  b. USN/USMC: Carrier Air Wing Rescue and Marine Expeditionary Force (MEF) aviation detachments for maritime recoveries.
  c. Allied CSAR contributions: RAAF/ROK allied rescue assets integrated per LOA.

4.3 CSAR Frequencies and Comms.
  a. CSAR Primary Guard Net (UHF): 280.000 MHz AM — monitored by all air and maritime assets as CSAR guard.
  b. CSAR VHF Guard: 123.450 MHz FM (exercise non-IFR broadcast for SAR coordination).
  c. Rescue Coord Net (SATCOM Priority): INMARSAT-EXER-1 (Simulated: 2.5 kHz L-band) — for survivor data and long-haul coordination.
  d. Beacons and homing: ELT/PLB homing to 121.5/406 MHz will be included in SAR localization; receivers will be equipped with directional locators. All participants must enable encrypted survivability comms where available (e.g., PRC-163 with SATCOM patch).

4.4 CSAR Employment Procedures.
  a. Immediate Action: On pilot down, nearest aircraft will set CSAR guard channel to 280.000 MHz and report position/time to TRCC within 2 minutes. TRCC will push IR/SAR notifications to maritime forces and JOC.
  b. Rescue packages will use pre-approved ingress/egress lanes in ACO and will coordinate SEAD/escort with the suppression tasking authority.
  c. If airspace is denied/contested, CSAR will default to maritime-based recoveries (helicopter from surface combatants) and coordinate with maritime commander for maneuver.

5. SPACE SUPPORT
5.1 GPS Degradation / Spotty Service Warnings.
  a. Given the CONOPS and adversary EW/space-contest conditions, commanders must assume degraded and intermittent GPS navigation and timing during MDIX. The Space Support Element (SSE) and J5 will publish GPS Degradation Advisories on the Space Support Net (SSN) and via ACO not later than 30 minutes after detection.
  b. Adversary EW injection and localized GPS denial will be categorized:
     - Tier 1: Degraded GPS (loss of integrity/position jumps) — advisory.
     - Tier 2: Denied GPS (localized jamming over ROZ-02/ROZ-03) — limitation on GPS-reliant weapons; alternate nav required.
     - Tier 3: Spoofing suspected — immediate stand-down of autonomous weapons requiring positive nav confirm.
  c. Mitigation. Units must carry and be proficient in alternate navigation: INS, celestial, LORAN-like backup training, and map/compass coastal navigation for rotary wings. All GPS-dependent munitions require a validated contingency plan if Tier 2/3 is declared.

5.2 SATCOM Priorities and Management.
  a. SATCOM channels are a constrained resource; priorities reflect strategic tasking: (1) JFC/C2 and JOC, (2) ISR/OPIR data flow for COP, (3) CSAR and lifesaving comms, (4) logistics/sustainment messages, (5) exercise admin and media.
  b. SATCOM Allocation:
     - Primary SATCOM (UHF SATCOM) — exercise primary: UHF SATCOM NET A (dynamic assignment by SATCOM Cell). Use only for C2 and time-sensitive ISR push.
     - Secondary SATCOM (MIL-Ka/Ku LEO): Commercial Ka/Ku augmentation allowed under CAAs; all use must be routed through the Space Support Cell to authorize and schedule bandwidth. Forced denial or reallocation will be preannounced when possible.
  c. SATCOM Anti-Jam. Units with anti-jam SATCOM terminals (protected SATCOM waveforms, DAMA, and Link-16 SATCOM extension) will be prioritized for critical data feeds. Where available, Protected Tactical SATCOM (PTS) is the baseline for high-importance C2 links.

5.3 OPIR (Overhead Persistent Infrared) and SSA Data Feeds.
  a. OPIR and space-based ISR feeds are integrated into the Joint All-Domain Command and Control (JADC2) COP. The Space Cell will disseminate OPIR cueing and SSA correlation via the Space Data Dissemination Net (SDDN).
  b. Data flow priority: Tactical warning (missile/ballistic threats), Maritime COP updates (surface track handover), and high-confidence ISR cueing for strike packages. Units must subscribe to the SDDN at mission pre-brief.
  c. Contested Space Contingency Procedures. If OPIR/space feeds are degraded, alternate cueing will be provided by airborne ISR (E-8, JSTARS-like), maritime deck sensors, and partner national assets per the ISR Collection Plan.

5.4 Spectrum & Space Emissions Control.
  a. All space-based transmissions and uplink commands must be coordinated through the Space Support Cell to avoid deconfliction and OPSEC breaches. Jamming or emissions used as red-team activity will be scheduled and promulgated in ACO.

6. COMMUNICATIONS
6.1 General Architecture. MDIX will employ a layered comms architecture emphasizing resilience: line-of-sight (LOS) VHF/UHF nets for tactical control, HF for long-haul redundancy, protected SATCOM for high-priority C2, and data-mesh/resilient tactical radio (e.g., Soldier/Battlefield radio waveforms) for ground/maritime distributed nodes. All comms use for exercise are unauthenticated/fictive where indicated unless pre-authorized.

6.2 Primary and Backup Frequency Nets (exercise allocations - not for release outside MDIX participants).
  a. JFC/JOC C2 Nets
     - Primary JOC SATCOM: PTS-EXER-01 (encrypted, assigned by Space Cell) — SatCOM channel pool (refer to Appendix COMMS-01)
     - Backup JOC HF: 8.136 MHz USB (HF long-haul JOC backup)
  b. Air Tasking and Control Nets
     - Air Tasking Net (ATN) Primary: UHF LOS 262.725 MHz AM (ATO sync and dynamic re-tasking)
     - ATN Backup: VHF Guard 136.625 MHz AM (local AOC to TACC)
     - Tactical Air Control Party (TACP) Ground-Air: VHF FM 30.780 MHz
  c. Air-to-Air
     - Tactical Air-to-Air: UHF FM 251.000 MHz (Link-16 gateway assigned per unit)
     - Link-16 Network: NET 1 — Crypto fill per component; JTIDS terminal scheduling via COMMO CELL.
  d. Maritime Nets
     - Primary Surface: HF 8414 kHz (USB) — secure long-haul maritime coordination
     - Ship-to-Ship Short-Range: VHF-FM 156.800 MHz (Channel 16) with exercise call-sign prefix "EX-"
  e. CSAR/Rescue
     - Primary CSAR Guard: UHF 280.000 MHz AM
     - CSAR Secondary: VHF 123.450 MHz FM
  f. EW/EMCON Control
     - EMCON Control Net (secure SATCOM): EMCON-CTRL-1 (broadcast enforced EMCON levels, jamming events, and authorized emissions)
     - EW Reporting Net (Unclassified): HF 5680 kHz USB.

6.3 Net Discipline and Call Signs.
  a. Net discipline is mandatory. Use brevity codes and standard phraseology per current US Joint Publications. Plain Language is preferred for multi-national interoperability unless crypto is pre-briefed.
  b. Exercise callsign conventions: Component prefix (e.g., "PACFLT-", "PACAF-") + mission type (e.g., "STRIKE", "TANKER", "CSAR") + numeric suffix. Example: PACAF-STRIKE-01, PACFLT-SHIP-05, JOC-CTRL-1.

6.4 EMCON and Anti-Jam Procedures.
  a. EMCON levels will be posted by the EMCON Authority and published in the ACO and COMMS Annex. Authorized EMCON deviations required for safety or mission-essential comms must be approved by the JOC.
  b. Anti-jam. Units will use frequency-hopping, spread-spectrum, and directional comms where available. Mesh and LPI/LPD waveforms will be preferred for distributed nodes. If jamming suspected, units will shift to pre-briefed alternate frequencies and report jamming source (bearing, strength) to the EW cell within 2 minutes.

6.5 COMSEC and OPSEC.
  a. All participants must follow COMSEC procedures; exercise-specific keying instructions are issued through the COMSEC account managers. Exercise comms designated UNCLASSIFIED simulation nets will still use discipline to avoid release of operationally sensitive data.
  b. OPSEC. Do not broadcast ship homeports, force numbers, or assured logistics schedules on unsecure nets. Use secure channels for logistics and force posture details.

ANNEXES (Reference Only — not repeated here):
  - COMMS-01: SATCOM Allocation Matrix (daily slotting)
  - ATO/ACO Sample: Daily Airspace Control Order Template
  - ROE Annex A: Rules of Engagement and Escalation Matrix
  - ISR Collection Plan: Priority ISR Cueing and Data Feed Procedures
  - CSAR Annex: Detailed Rescue Procedures, Medical Evacuation Routing, and Host Nation Coordination

REPORTING AND COORDINATION:
  - All incidents, PID disputes, declared jamming, satellite denial events, or CIVCAS incidents must be reported via the JOC SITREP Net and logged in the Theater COP within 15 minutes.
  - Component liaisons (J3/J5) will maintain 24/7 representation in the JOC for MDIX. Tactical coordination will occur on designated nets listed above.
  - Any request for SPINS deviation requires written justification and will be considered by J5/J3; emergency verbal approvals may be granted and must be followed by formal request within 2 hours.

AUTHORITY:
  - These SPINS are promulgated under the authority of CDRUSINDOPACOM per the JSCP and supporting theater planning documents (NDS Extract, NMS Theater Annex, CONPLAN/OPLAN). Changes or rescindment will be issued by J5.

SECURITY WARNING:
  - This document is UNCLASSIFIED // FOUO. Dissemination is limited to personnel with a need-to-know for exercise participation. Unauthorized disclosure may degrade exercise realism and operational security.

POINTS OF CONTACT:
  - Theater J5 SPINS Cell: + (exercise-only satcom channel assigned) / spains.cell@indopacom.mil (exercise mailbox)
  - JOC Communications Cell: COMMS-JOC (satcom primary — PTS-EXER-01)
  - Space Support Cell: space.support@indopacom.mil (assignments and GPS advisories)

End of SPINS.",

{"title":"UNITED STATES INDO-PACIFIC COMMAND AIRSPACE CONTROL ORDER (ACO)","docType":"ACO","content":"UNCLASSIFIED // FOR OFFICIAL USE ONLY
UNITED STATES INDO-PACIFIC COMMAND
AIRSPACE CONTROL ORDER (ACO)
OPR: J3–Air / Combined Air Operations Center (CAOC) INDOPACOM
EFFECTIVE PERIOD: 01 MAR 2026 0001Z — 08 MAR 2026 2359Z
REFERENCES: JP 3-52; JP 3-30; JSCP INDOPACOM MDIX tasking 01 MAR 2026; CONPLAN/OPLAN INDOPACOM SHIELD

1. GENERAL
1.1 Purpose. This Airspace Control Order (ACO) implements airspace control measures to support USINDOPACOM Multi-Domain Integration Exercise (MDIX) and associated contested logistics / degraded space readiness activities in the Western Pacific theater, 01–08 Mar 2026. It apportions, reserves, restricts, and coordinates airspace for joint and combined air, maritime, space-support, cyberspace, and information operations consistent with theater objectives DENY, DEGRADE, PROTECT, SUSTAIN, DESTROY as directed by the NDS Extract and NMS Theater Annex.
1.2 Authority. This ACO is published under authority of Commander, United States Indo-Pacific Command (CDRUSINDOPACOM) and executed by the Combined Air Operations Center (CAOC) at Andersen (Andersen CAOC callsign: PAC-CAOC), with Tactical Air Control Party (TACP), Maritime Airspace Coordination, and component airspace managers. All airspace users will comply with the controlling agencies and procedures listed herein.
1.3 Applicability. Applies to all US/Allied military aircraft, unmanned aircraft systems (UAS), contracted airlift, and participating civilian aircraft supporting MDIX. Non-exercise non-participating aircraft shall coordinate through appropriate diplomatic/overflight channels and obtain permission prior to entry.
1.4 Control Measures Summary. This ACO establishes Restricted Operating Zones (ROZs), Air Refueling Tracks (AR), Combat Air Patrol (CAP) stations, Transit Corridors (TC), and Kill Boxes (KB). All aircraft will carry current ATO/ATRS appendices, use designated frequencies, and comply with Identification Friend or Foe (IFF) code management and authentication procedures directed by PAC-CAOC.
1.5 Degraded Space/Communications Procedures. Anticipating degraded space-enabled services, CAOC implements a prioritized secure HF/UHF/VHF/tactical SATCOM fallback plan. Primary C2: UHF LOS (72.100–76.000 MHz Guard/selcal as per annex). Secondary: HF P2P net (6.209 MHz AM). SATCOM: Protected X-band (COMSEC required) only for authenticated net participants. EMCON restrictions in select ROZs (see ROZs) will limit emissions; scheduled periodic beacon bursts for identification will occur on 243.000 MHz discrete times listed in Table A (ATO Annex).
1.6 Authentication. Use three-part authentication: (1) callsign + mission code (per ATO), (2) two-word challenge-response from current authentication roster, (3) IFF mode/code verification. Failure to authenticate triggers immediate interception procedures or denial of airspace entry.
1.7 Coordination. All component airspace managers (PACAF A3, USFF Airspace, MARFORPAC, USARPAC aviation liaison) coordinate via the CAOC airspace cell. Real-time deconfliction provided by CAOC Airspace Battle Manager (ABM) on primary controlling frequency 282.000 MHz UHF (ABM callsign: PAC-ABM). Emergency diversion approvals via PAC-CAOC Commander (Andersen) or on-scene Tactical Director.

2. RESTRICTED OPERATING ZONES (ROZ)
General ROZ procedures: Entry prohibited without written approval from PAC-CAOC or on-scene Airspace Coordinator (OSC). ROZ activation times may be modified by NOTAM via CAOC. Coordinates in WGS-84; altitudes MSL unless noted.

ROZ-01 "TSHIELD-SOUTH" (South China Sea — Exercise Close-In)
- Center: 15°30.00'N 115°00.00'E
- Radius: 120 NM (approximate polygon defined in Annex A)
- Vertical limits: Surface — FL600
- Effective: 01 Mar 2026 0001Z — 08 Mar 2026 2359Z (continuous)
- Purpose: Live-fire air-to-surface, integration with maritime anti-access denial (A2/AD) suppression.
- Restrictions: No transit without CAOC approval. UAS operations limited to authorized exercise elements. Emissions control level EMCON-B unless specifically scheduled windows for identification bursts at 0200Z and 1400Z daily on 243.000 MHz.
- Controlling Agency: PAC-CAOC (Andersen) / ABM
- Safety/Procedures: All weapons release within ROZ-01 require positive battle damage assessment coordination via Strike Control (STRIKE-CON callsign PAC-STRIKE). Minimum safe altitude for non-exercise flights 20,000 ft. Surface-to-air live-fire lanes separated; see Live Fire Safety Annex.

ROZ-02 "LUZON-FACILITATION" (Luzon Strait — Logistics Hub Protection)
- Coordinates: Polygon ABCD (N 19°30.00'–N 20°30.00'; E 121°30.00'–E 122°45.00')
- Vertical limits: Surface — 15,000 ft
- Effective: 01 Mar 2026 0001Z — 08 Mar 2026 2359Z (periodic access windows for allied transport)
- Purpose: Secure corridors for exercise logistics (sealift/airlift staging) and contested port operations rehearsal.
- Restrictions: Non-exercise scheduled transports granted corridor pass times (coord via PAC-LOGNET). All aircraft must maintain discrete TACAN channel 60X and monitor 251.200 MHz.
- Controlling Agency: PACAF Air Mobility Liaison (AMSL) / PAC-CAOC

ROZ-03 "TAIWAN-STRAIT-WARN" (Area proximate to Taiwan Strait — elevated ID procedures)
- Coordinates: 23°30.00'N 120°00.00'E to 25°30.00'N 122°30.00'E (see Annex A)
- Vertical limits: Surface — FL350
- Effective: 01 Mar 2026 0001Z — 08 Mar 2026 2359Z
- Purpose: High-risk area for increased monitoring and interceptor presence. Not for live weapons unless specifically authorized by CDRUSINDOPACOM.
- Restrictions: All transit requires corridor assignment (see Transit Corridors). Positive control mandatory. IFF Mode 4/5/X maintained. Identification procedures include scheduled AIS bursts at 1100Z/2300Z on 243.000 MHz and encrypted challenge on 30.350 MHz HF.
- Controlling Agency: PAC-CAOC / Combined TACC Manila (coordination cell) for combined operations.

ROZ-04 "MARIANAS-TRAIN" (Marianas — Integrated Air Defense Training)
- Center: 13°30.00'N 145°30.00'E
- Radius: 80 NM
- Vertical limits: Surface — FL450
- Effective: 01 Mar 2026 0001Z — 08 Mar 2026 2359Z
- Purpose: Integrated air defense exercise; includes simulated anti-ship missile engagements. Selective EMCON; scheduled radar windows for combined tracking nets.
- Restrictions: Civilian traffic rerouted; emergency landings coordinated through Andersen Tower (AND TWR).
- Controlling Agency: Andersen CAOC Coordination Cell / PAC-ADCON

3. AIR REFUELING TRACKS (AR)
General AR procedures: All tanker operations operate in positive control environment. All tankers publish fuel off/on times in ATO. Tanker on-station time limits based on contested logistics plan; tankers will monitor primary refueling frequency and guard.

AR-01 "NEPTUNE-AR1" (Luzon Str. – South China Sea refueling track)
- Track: J-shaped track between waypoints WP1 19°00.00'N 122°00.00'E — WP2 18°00.00'N 120°30.00'E — WP3 16°30.00'N 119°00.00'E
- Altitudes: Primary AR alt: FL200 — FL240 (tankers), receiver pre-contact alt FL220
- Effective: 01 Mar 2026 0001Z — 08 Mar 2026 2359Z (continuous ops; scheduled surge windows 0300–0900Z and 1500–2100Z)
- Tanker units: 5th Aerial Refueling Wing (KC-135R / KC-46A) — Callsign "NEPTUNE-KTR"
- Primary ATC freq: 306.800 MHz UHF (NEPTUNE-FREQ)
- Procedures: Pre-contact checklist compliance required. Receivers must establish communications and report planned offload in lbs. Tanker will issue pre-contact clearance; maximum 3 receivers on a basket concurrently. Contested-space contingency: if SATCOM unavailable, use HF 8.834 MHz AM as backup.
- Controlling Agency: PAC-CAOC Tanker Cell / NEPTUNE-KTR On-Scene Commander

AR-02 "MARINER-AR2" (Marianas — Guam/Andersen orbit)
- Track: Circular orbit centered 13°30.00'N 144°45.00'E radius 25 NM
- Altitudes: FL180 — FL220
- Effective: 01 Mar 2026 0001Z — 08 Mar 2026 2359Z
- Tanker units: 734 AES (KC-135/KC-46) — Callsign "MARINER"
- Freq: 318.700 MHz UHF
- Procedures: Closed-orbit refueling. Tankers maintain NORDO procedures; receivers must submit pre-brief via ATO FPL.

4. CAP STATIONS
General CAP procedures: Positive control from CAOC or delegated Combined Air Defense Commander (CADC). CAP handoff procedures defined in Annex D. Minimum separation and altitude deconfliction for CAPs and air refueling stacks mandated.

CAP-Alpha "TAIWAN-CAP"
- Location: Patrol center 24°10.00'N 121°30.00'E (variable patrol box)
- Patrol Box: 60 NM radial, sector 030°–150°
- Altitudes: FL250 — FL350
- Primary Unit: 18th Wing (F-22A / F-35A mix) — Callsign "ALPHA-01/ALPHA-ROSTER"
- On-station times: 2-hour rotations; surge capability 1-hour
- Frequencies: Tactical uplink 281.200 MHz UHF (ALPHA-TAC); Guard 243.000 MHz
- Rules of Engagement (ROE): Intercept-only status unless positive hostile intent observed or weapons release authorized by CAOC/PAC-STRIKE. Visual ID required before engagement unless missile launch or hostile fire directed against friendly forces.
- Identification: IFF Mode 5/X required. CAP must coordinate with maritime on-scene commander when within 30 NM of surface combatants.

CAP-Bravo "LUZON-CAP"
- Location: 20°00.00'N 122°00.00'E
- Altitudes: FL200 — FL300
- Primary Unit: Marine Air Group (F/A-18E/F, F-35B) — Callsign "BRAVO"
- Freq: 265.300 MHz UHF
- Procedures: CAP-BRAVO responsible for escort of exercise strategic airlift in ROZ-02 windows. Positive control mandatory.

CAP-Charlie "MARIANAS-CAP"
- Location: 13°30.00'N 145°30.00'E (Andersen proximate)
- Altitudes: FL220 — FL360
- Primary Unit: PACAF Air Defense Squadron / Air National Guard (F-15EX) — Callsign "CHARLIE"
- Freq: 270.600 MHz UHF
- Procedures: Defensive counter-air; priority on detection/tracking of medium-range ballistic missile (MRBM) signatures. Immediate handoff to Space/STRIKE when launching adversary hypersonic simulation detected.

5. TRANSIT CORRIDORS
General: Transit Corridors provide safe passage for logistics, command movement, and emergency egress. Corridors feature fixed lateral boundaries and altitude blocks. All corridor traffic must file flight plan via PAC-FLIGHT (Secure Link) and monitor corridor frequencies. Unauthorized deviation subject to interception.

TC-01 "LUZON-LIBERTY" (North–South transit)
- Corridor centerline: 21°30.00'N 121°00.00'E to 16°00.00'N 120°00.00'E
- Width: ±15 NM
- Altitudes: Surface — FL200 (civil transports below FL200); FL200+ reserved for tactical transit
- Purpose: Routine airlift and tanker repositioning.
- Freq: 251.200 MHz UHF (TC-LUZON)
- Procedures: Fixed schedule windows listed in ATO (daily 0300–0800Z; 1500–1900Z). All aircraft must report position every 30 minutes on corridor frequency and update fuel state. In degraded space scenario, HF backup 6.209 MHz.

TC-02 "TAIWAN-STRAIT-CORRIDOR" (East–West limited transit)
- Centerline: 24°30.00'N 121°45.00'E to 24°30.00'N 123°45.00'E
- Width: ±10 NM
- Altitudes: Surface — FL150
- Purpose: Controlled transit for surface force air support and limited diplomacy flights.
- Authority: Entry requires slot from PAC-CAOC and adherence to authentication. Non-military civil transit suspended during specific exercise events.

TC-03 "MARIANAS-ARC" (Marianas to Guam logistic route)
- Track: 13°00.00'N 143°00.00'E to 13°30.00'N 145°30.00'E
- Width: 20 NM
- Altitudes: Surface — FL280
- Purpose: Sustainment transit between supply nodes and Andersen/Apra harbor.
- Freq: 260.150 MHz UHF (TC-MARIANA)
- Procedures: Cargo aircraft must declare hazardous cargo and fuel state. Contested logistics procedures: low-observable approaches scheduled to minimize detection; see Logistics Annex.

6. KILL BOXES (KB)
General: Kill Boxes are pre-deconflicted three-dimensional areas that facilitate the integration of joint fires and minimize coordination burden. All kinetic fires in Blue Kill Boxes must have positive clearance from Strike Control. Red Kill Boxes represent permissive engagement for defensive strikes against identified adversary aerial or maritime threats. Blue Kill Boxes used for offensive surface-to-surface and air-to-surface fires to achieve DENY/DEGRADE objectives. Engagement constraints and CDE (Collateral Damage Estimates) apply per Weapon Safety Annex.

KB-B1 "SCS-B1-BLUE"
- Designation: Blue Kill Box B1 (South China Sea offensive integration)
- Coordinates: polygon points (Annex A)
- Vertical limits: Surface — FL400
- Effective: 01 Mar 2026 0200Z — 08 Mar 2026 2200Z (daily windows; see ATO)
- Engagement Rules:
  - Purpose: Integrated air, maritime, and long-range fires to degrade adversary A2/AD nodes (simulated).
  - Weapons: Air-to-surface, maritime cruise missiles (exercise-representative), surface-to-surface fires permitted.
  - Clearance: Strike Control (PAC-STRIKE) positive clearance required 10 minutes prior to weapons release. Deconfliction: No friendly aircraft within 30 NM radius of designated aimpoint within 10 minutes of strike unless coordinated.
  - Electromagnetic Emissions: Jamming permitted within KB-B1; EMCON level DEGRADE authorized.
  - Battle Damage Assessment: ISR assets (UAS/SSRS) assigned BDA windows; priority to CAOC Collection Manager.

KB-R1 "TAIWAN-R1-RED"
- Designation: Red Kill Box R1 (Taiwan approaches — defensive)
- Coordinates: 24°00.00'N 120°30.00'E to 25°00.00'N 121°30.00'E
- Vertical limits: Surface — FL350
- Effective: Continuous during ACO effective period
- Engagement Rules:
  - Purpose: Defensive engagement against hostile air or surface platforms threatening friendly forces or critical nodes.
  - Weapons: All defensive weapons systems (air-to-air, surface-to-air, surface-to-surface) may engage positively identified hostile tracks without additional strike clearance if the hostile exhibits hostile intent or hostile act per ROE.
  - Positive Identification: Visual or sensor positive ID required except where immediate lethal threat observed (e.g., inbound missile within 60 seconds).
  - Reporting: All engagements must be reported to PAC-ADCON and CAOC within 5 minutes on 282.000 MHz with track number, weapon employed, effect. Post-engagement BDA coordination mandatory.

KB-B2 "Luzon-KB2-BLUE"
- Coordinates: See Annex A polygon centered near 18°30.00'N 121°00.00'E
- Vertical limits: Surface — FL450
- Effective: 02 Mar 2026 0400Z — 07 Mar 2026 2000Z
- Engagement Rules:
  - Purpose: Interdiction of simulated adversary surface logistics; integrate maritime strike and air-to-surface fires.
  - Allocation: Priority to joint suppression of enemy air defenses (J-SEAD) packages. SEAD packages must coordinate airspace with AR tracks to avoid refueling conflicts. CAOC to assign clearance windows.

7. AIRSPACE MANAGEMENT PROCEDURES & FREQUENCIES
7.1 Primary Controlling Agencies and Callsigns:
- PAC-CAOC/Combined Air Operations Center (Andersen): PAC-CAOC (Primary controlling for this ACO)
- Airspace Battle Manager (ABM): PAC-ABM (callsign)
- Strike Control: PAC-STRIKE
- Tanker On-Scene Commander: NEPTUNE-KTR / MARINER
- Logistics/Movement Control: PAC-LOGNET
- Air Defense Control: PAC-ADCON
7.2 Frequencies (primary/backup):
- PAC-CAOC Control: 282.000 MHz UHF (primary)
- ABM Tactical: 271.100 MHz UHF
- Strike Control: 305.400 MHz UHF
- Tanker Primary: 306.800 MHz UHF (AR-01)
- CAP Alpha Tac: 281.200 MHz UHF
- Guard: 243.000 MHz (IFF bursts per schedule)
- HF Backup: 6.209 MHz / 8.834 MHz AM
- SATCOM Protected: X-band net (authentication required)
7.3 Deconfliction Procedures:
- All units must file ATO/ADIZ updates per ATO timeline. Changes through PAC-CAOC only. Emergency deviations require immediate notification to ABM on 282.000 MHz.
- Minimum lateral and vertical separation: 3 NM / 500 ft in terminal; 5 NM / 1,000 ft in enroute; exceptions require positive control approval.
7.4 Air-to-Air Intercept Procedures:
- On-sight intercepts conducted per Intercept Rules of the Air Annex. Interceptors to attempt visual ID and positive authentication. If intercept fails and track remains non-compliant, engage per ROE and KB designation if within Red KB.

8. C2 & REPORTING
8.1 Tactical Linkages. All participating platforms must maintain required data-links where operationally feasible: Link-16 (when available), MADL for stealth asset data exchange, and legacy voice nets. In degraded space scenarios, reliance shifts to HF voice and encrypted UHF/LOS nets.
8.2 Engagement Reporting. Any release of ordnance (including simulated) must be reported on CAS/Strike Report net within 5 minutes with the following: aircraft callsign, time, ordnance type, aimpoint coordinates, effect observed, friendly ordnance safety confirmation.
8.3 Incident Response. Airspace infringements or unauthorized airspace entries: ABM immediately directs intercept. CAOC initiates incident assessment and notifies CDRUSINDOPACOM J3.

9. LOGISTICS & SUSTAINMENT SUPPORT
9.1 Airbase Usage. Andersen AFB and Clark AB scheduled as primary hubs for exercise surge. Access to forward expeditionary airfields (FAE) requires AMSL approval and coordination with PAC-LOGNET.
9.2 Fuel Prioritization. Tanker allocation follows the JSCP sustainment apportionment: Strategic airlift > CAP sustainment > ISR > permissive strike. Fuel states reported in pounds; orders for refuel priority logged in tanker cell.

10. AMENDMENTS & SUSPENSION
10.1 Amendments. CAOC may amend this ACO by authenticated message. Emergency temporary restrictions may be declared by on-scene commanders and must be reported to CAOC within 15 minutes.
10.2 Suspension. CDRUSINDOPACOM holds authority to suspend any element of this ACO should strategic or operational conditions warrant, including escalation by adversary beyond exercise parameters.

11. COORDINATION & DISTRIBUTION
11.1 This ACO will be distributed to all component commands, combined/coalition partners participating in MDIX, host nation airspace authorities, and appropriate civil aviation authorities via DIPLO channels. All units must acknowledge receipt and understanding within 2 hours of publication.
11.2 Points of Contact:
- PAC-CAOC Commander (Andersen): COM +1-670-555-1000, TAC 282.000 MHz
- Airspace Battle Manager (PAC-ABM): COM +1-670-555-1100, TAC 271.100 MHz
- Strike Control (PAC-STRIKE): COM +1-670-555-1200, TAC 305.400 MHz
- Logistics Cell (PAC-LOGNET): COM +1-670-555-1300, TAC 251.200 MHz

ANNEXES (attached to ACO; summarized references below):
- Annex A: ROZ/Kill Box polygons and precise waypoint coordinates (WGS-84)
- Annex B: Authentication roster and challenge-response schedules
- Annex C: Live Fire Safety and Range Control Measures

Operation: INDOPACOM SHIELD — Western Pacific MDIX
ATO Cycle: 01 (Exercise)
Effective: 01 MAR 2026 0001Z – 08 MAR 2026 2400Z
Classification: UNCLASSIFIED // FOUO (Exercise Construct)

REFERENCES (Exercise): JP 3-30, JP 3-52, JP 3-14, JP 4-0; USINDOPACOM MDIX OPLAN extract; MDIX JIPTL (sanitized).

SITUATION (Exercise Summary)
MDIX simulates a near-peer Pacific adversary employing an A2/AD network, contested EMS/cyber, and degraded space-enabled services to restrict friendly freedom of action. Friendly forces execute distributed air operations with constrained logistics, intermittent SATCOM, PNT degradation, and ISR latency injects. All targets, identifiers, and effects are simulated; no real-world target prosecution is implied.

ASSIGNED/FORCES AVAILABLE (MDIX ORBAT; exercise call signs are generic)
- 388 FW: 24x F-35A (Kadena AB)
- 35 FW: 18x F-16C (Misawa AB)
- CVW-5: 36x F/A-18E (embarked CVN-76)
- 55 WG: 4x RC-135V (Kadena AB)
- Maritime Fires (non-sortie joint effects, coordinated in ATO/ACO as needed): DESRON-15 (5x DDG), SUBRON-15 (3x SSN)
- Simulated enablers (EXCON-provided for MDIX realism): E-3G “SENTRY” (AWACS), KC-46A/KC-135R “TANKER,” EA support “RAVEN” (stand-in non-kinetic effects), CSAR alert “ANGEL” (exercise recovery)

PLANNING ASSUMPTIONS (for sortie accounting)
- “Sortie” = one aircraft mission. Multi-role sorties are counted once and credited to the supported JIPTL priority/effect.
- Degraded comms require time-based control and pre-planned triggers; dynamic retasking is limited to windows identified in Section 4.
- Daily sustainable sortie capacity (combat-coded, not counting simulated enablers):
  • F-35A: 28 sorties/day sustained (surge to 34 Days 1–2)
  • F-16C: 22 sorties/day sustained (surge to 26 Days 1–2)
  • F/A-18E: 48 sorties/day sustained (surge to 54 Days 1–3)
  • RC-135V: 4 sorties/day (2 aircraft available for daily coverage, 2 in depth maintenance/alert)
- Total fighter capacity (sustained): 98 sorties/day; surge early: up to 114 sorties/day.
- RC-135 is treated as theater ISR and allocated across priorities by collection focus.

JIPTL PRIORITIES (sanitized target sets and intended effects)
Priority 1 (P1): DENY/DESTROY — Theater A2/AD Node Cluster (IADS sensors/engagement nodes, coastal defense nodes, operational C2 nodes) [BE 0101–0110 simulated]
Priority 2 (P2): DENY/DEGRADE — Adversary Air & ISR Generation (fighter operating locations, command posts for air tasking, non-kinetic ISR relay nodes)
Priority 3 (P3): DENY/DESTROY — Maritime Power Projection (surface action group cueing, amphib staging nodes, maritime strike C2)
Priority 4 (P4): DEGRADE — Information/Networked Kill Chain (data fusion nodes, comm relay points, cyber/EMS coordination cells; primary effects are non-kinetic within exercise)
Priority 5 (P5): PROTECT/SUSTAIN — Friendly Force Protection & Logistics Corridor Assurance (DCA, escort of high-value airborne assets, protection of hubs, combat air patrols along sea/air LOCs)

--------------------------------------------------------------------
1. COMMANDER’S GUIDANCE
--------------------------------------------------------------------
1.1 Commander’s Intent (Exercise)
Establish and maintain local air superiority sufficient to (1) deny adversary effective A2/AD employment, (2) prevent adversary air and maritime power projection in the exercise operating area, and (3) preserve friendly freedom of maneuver and sustainment under contested logistics and degraded space services. Success is measured by demonstrated ability to plan, execute, and assess multi-domain effects under comm/PNT degradation, not by massed strike counts.

1.2 Operational Emphasis
a. Priority of effort by phase:
- Phase 1 (Days 1–3): P1 then P5 then P2. Objective: create operating windows (suppression), establish DCA baseline, and reduce adversary counterair response.
- Phase 2 (Days 4–7): P2 and P3 with sustained pressure on P1. Objective: constrain adversary sortie generation and maritime maneuver while degrading the kill chain (P4).
- Phase 3 (Day 8+): P4 and dynamic targeting; maintain P5. Objective: exploit ISR-driven opportunities and demonstrate resilient C2/ATO agility.

b. Main supporting effort throughout: preserve high-value airborne assets (HVAA) and logistics flow; avoid mission-kill of tankers/ISR in the scenario.

1.3 Restrictions / Constraints (Exercise Safety & Policy)
- All effects are simulated and must remain within EXCON-approved target sets and rules.
- No real-world geolocation, frequencies, weapon employment parameters, or TTP specifics will be published in MAAP/ATO products beyond exercise control measures.
- Civil air traffic deconfliction is mandatory. Use ACO measures; if comms degrade, execute pre-briefed “lost comm” timing gates and altitude blocks per ACO.
- Space degradation injects are expected. Missions requiring precision timing/target mensuration will be planned inside “precision engagement windows” (Section 4) or will use non-precision simulated effects with commander approval.
- Minimize single-point-of-failure C2: pre-plan mission packages with autonomous execution triggers.

1.4 Risk Tolerance
- Moderate risk to mission accomplishment accepted to preserve force (aircraft and HVAA) and to protect sustainment nodes.
- Low tolerance for loss of tankers/AWACS/ISR platforms in the scenario; DCA and escort are mandatory when threat conditions are “AMBER/RED” (as injected).
- Acceptable risk: short-duration gaps in continuous CAP if required to enable P1 suppression windows, provided base defense and early warning are adequate.

1.5 Apportionment (Daily, adjustable by JFACC)
- Phase 1 baseline: 35% P1, 15% P2, 10% P3, 5% P4, 35% P5.
- Phase 2 baseline: 20% P1, 25% P2, 20% P3, 10% P4, 25% P5.
- Phase 3 baseline: 10% P1, 15% P2, 15% P3, 30% P4, 30% P5.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
2. SORTIE ALLOCATION MATRIX
--------------------------------------------------------------------
2.1 Sortie Allocation by Priority (Mission Types and Platforms)
Note: “RAVEN” indicates stand-in non-kinetic/EW effects executed by organic fighters or simulated external support; counted as fighter sorties when flown by F-35/F-16/F/A-18.

PRIORITY 1 (P1) — A2/AD Node Cluster (DENY/DESTROY)
Mission types needed:
- SEAD/DEAD (simulated suppression/destruction)
- Escort (fighters)
- ISR cueing / EW support (RC-135 focus; RAVEN)
Platforms:
- F-35A (primary), F/A-18E (secondary), F-16C (secondary), RC-135V (cueing)
Sorties per day (by phase):
- Phase 1 (D1–D3): 30/day (20x F-35A, 8x F/A-18E, 2x F-16C; RC-135 focus 1 sortie/day)
- Phase 2 (D4–D7): 18/day (10x F-35A, 6x F/A-18E, 2x F-16C; RC-135 focus 0.5 sortie/day equivalent)
- Phase 3 (D8+): 10/day (6x F-35A, 3x F/A-18E, 1x F-16C; RC-135 focus as needed)

PRIORITY 2 (P2) — Adversary Air & ISR Generation (DENY/DEGRADE)
Mission types needed:
- OCA (simulated airbase/air operations node attack)
- Fighter sweep / counterair pressure
- ISR and battle damage/effects confirmation (RC-135 prioritization during windows)
Platforms:
- F-35A (primary), F-16C (primary), F/A-18E (secondary), RC-135V (collection)
Sorties per day:
- Phase 1: 14/day (6x F-35A, 6x F-16C, 2x F/A-18E; RC-135 0.5 sortie/day focus)
- Phase 2: 24/day (8x F-35A, 10x F-16C, 6x F/A-18E; RC-135 1 sortie/day focus)
- Phase 3: 14/day (4x F-35A, 6x F-16C, 4x F/A-18E; RC-135 as available)

PRIORITY 3 (P3) — Maritime Power Projection (DENY/DESTROY)
Mission types needed:
- Maritime strike (simulated)
- Surface search/cueing (RC-135 maritime emitters as available; space ISR windowing)
- Defensive counter-maritime escort (fighters)
Platforms:
- F/A-18E (primary), F-35A (secondary), F-16C (limited), RC-135V (cueing)
Sorties per day:
- Phase 1: 8/day (6x F/A-18E, 2x F-35A; RC-135 cueing as spillover)
- Phase 2: 18/day (12x F/A-18E, 4x F-35A, 2x F-16C; RC-135 0.5 sortie/day focus)
- Phase 3: 12/day (8x F/A-18E, 3x F-35A, 1x F-16C)

PRIORITY 4 (P4) — Information/Networked Kill Chain (DEGRADE)
Mission types needed:
- Non-kinetic support (simulated cyber/EMS, comm disruption, deception)
- ISR to characterize network activity (RC-135)
- Limited kinetic strike against relay nodes (simulated) when authorized by EXCON
Platforms:
- F-35A (sensing/EA stand-in), F/A-18E (stand-in), RC-135V (primary)
Sorties per day:
- Phase 1: 4/day (2x F-35A, 2x F/A-18E; RC-135 0.5 sortie/day focus)
- Phase 2: 10/day (4x F-35A, 4x F/A-18E, 2x F-16C as comm relay/escort; RC-135 1 sortie/day focus)
- Phase 3: 20/day (8x F-35A, 8x F/A-18E, 4x F-16C; RC-135 1–2 sorties/day focus)

PRIORITY 5 (P5) — Friendly Protection & Sustainment (PROTECT/SUSTAIN)
Mission types needed:
- DCA (CAPs over hubs/sea lanes), HVAA escort
- Counter-cruise missile / counter-ISR response (simulated)
- Base defense support (airborne presence; integrate with surface air defense in ACO)
Platforms:
- F-16C (primary), F/A-18E (primary), F-35A (secondary/rapid response), RC-135V (threat warning collection as available)
Sorties per day:
- Phase 1: 30/day (10x F-35A, 8x F-16C, 12x F/A-18E; RC-135 1 sortie/day focus for threat warning)
- Phase 2: 26/day (8x F-35A, 8x F-16C, 10x F/A-18E)
- Phase 3: 24/day (6x F-35A, 8x F-16C, 10x F/A-18E)

2.2 Daily Sortie Requirement vs Capacity (D1–D8)
Capacity below includes fighters + RC-135 actual; simulated tankers/AWACS are tracked in Flow Plan.

DAILY CAPACITY (planned)
- Day 1: 114 fighter + 4 RC-135 = 118 total
- Day 2: 114 fighter + 4 RC-135 = 118 total
- Day 3: 108 fighter + 4 RC-135 = 112 total
- Days 4–7: 98 fighter + 4 RC-135 = 102 total
- Day 8: 98 fighter + 4 RC-135 = 102 total

DAILY REQUIREMENT (planned tasked sorties; remainder held for alert/spares/reconstitution)
- Day 1: 96 tasked (88 fighters + 4 RC-135 + 4 flexible spares allocated as “mission-ready”)
- Day 2: 100 tasked (92 fighters + 4 RC-135 + 4 flexible spares)
- Day 3: 94 tasked (86 fighters + 4 RC-135 + 4 flexible spares)
- Day 4: 92 tasked (84 fighters + 4 RC-135 + 4 flexible spares)
- Day 5: 92 tasked (84 fighters + 4 RC-135 + 4 flexible spares)
- Day 6: 88 tasked (80 fighters + 4 RC-135 + 4 flexible spares)
- Day 7: 86 tasked (78 fighters + 4 RC-135 + 4 flexible spares)
- Day 8: 86 tasked (78 fighters + 4 RC-135 + 4 flexible spares)

Daily “available margin” (capacity minus tasked) is reserved for: abort re-fly, weather/space degradation re-attacks, surge DCA, and EXCON dynamic targeting events.

2.3 Daily Allocation by Priority (All sorties; fighters + RC-135 counted within the priority they support)
Numbers below are planned tasked sorties per day by priority; these are the primary drivers for ATO mission line development.

DAY 1 (01 MAR): P1 30 / P2 12 / P3 8 / P4 4 / P5 30  = 84 (plus 8 ISR/airborne C2/support allocations embedded; 4 spares)
DAY 2 (02 MAR): P1 32 / P2 14 / P3 8 / P4 4 / P5 32 = 90 (plus 6 embedded support; 4 spares)
DAY 3 (03 MAR): P1 28 / P2 16 / P3 8 / P4 4 / P5 28 = 84 (plus 6 embedded support; 4 spares)

DAY 4 (04 MAR): P1 18 / P2 24 / P3 16 / P4 8 / P5 26 = 92 (includes RC-135 focus shift to P2/P4)
DAY 5 (05 MAR): P1 18 / P2 24 / P3 18 / P4 6 / P5 26 = 92
DAY 6 (06 MAR): P1 18 / P2 22 / P3 18 / P4 8 / P5 22 = 88
DAY 7 (07 MAR): P1 16 / P2 22 / P3 18 / P4 8 / P5 22 = 86

DAY 8 (08 MAR): P1 10 / P2 14 / P3 12 / P4 20 / P5 24 = 80 (plus 6 embedded support/dynamic lines as directed; 4 spares)

Notes:
- “Embedded support” refers to sorties whose primary purpose is escort, EW stand-in, or on-call response but are counted within the supported priority. The ATO will still publish explicit roles per mission line.
- RC-135 tasking: 4 sorties/day total; allocation emphasis by day:
  • D1: 2 sorties P1, 1 sortie P5, 1 sortie P2
  • D2: 2 sorties P1, 1 sortie P2, 1 sortie P5
  • D3: 1 sortie P1, 2 sorties P2, 1 sortie P5
  • D4–D7: 1 sortie P2, 1 sortie P4, 1 sortie P3 (maritime cueing), 1 sortie P5 (threat warning)
  • D8: 2 sorties P4, 1 sortie P2, 1 sortie P5

--------------------------------------------------------------------
3. PHASE EMPLOYMENT CONCEPT
--------------------------------------------------------------------
PHASE 1 (Days 1–3): Initial Strikes, SEAD, DCA Establishment
Purpose: Create operational windows by suppressing the A2/AD network (P1), while immediately establishing a resilient DCA posture (P5) to protect hubs and HVAA under comm and PNT stress.

Key tasks:
- P1: Execute two daily suppression “windows” (W1 and W2) against simulated IADS/sensor/engagement clusters sufficient to open corridors for follow-on counterair and maritime effects. Primary emphasis is on reversible suppression and time-bound denial rather than permanent destruction (exercise realism and escalation control).
- P5: Establish continuous DCA presence with minimum two CAP orbits covering (a) primary air hub approach sector and (b) maritime LOC sector. CAP continuity is maintained by time-based handovers if datalink is degraded.
- P2: Begin counterair pressure and simulated strikes on air ops nodes to slow adversary response cycles.
- P3: Limited early maritime shaping—deny adversary reconnaissance-to-strike sequence rather than attempting full maritime neutralization.
- P4: Minimal initial non-kinetic shaping; prioritize collection and characterization to set conditions for Phase 2/3.

Operational design (per day):
- Two main mission pushes, aligned to “precision engagement windows” (Section 4):
  • Push A (approx 0200Z–0800Z): primary P1 suppression + DCA refresh
  • Push B (approx 1400Z–2000Z): P2 counterair + limited P3 maritime shaping + P1 re-suppression as required
- Between pushes: maintain CAP and on-call alert; prioritize aircraft recovery, maintenance, and rearm under contested logistics injects.

PHASE 2 (Days 4–7): Sustained Operations, Deep Strike
Purpose: Maintain pressure on adversary force generation (P2) and maritime power projection (P3) while sustaining a “good enough” suppression level on A2/AD (P1) and increasing kill-chain degradation (P4).

Key tasks:
- P2: Daily rhythm of counterair pressure and simulated strikes against air generation nodes during windows that minimize blue exposure and maximize operational impact. Objective is measurable reduction in adversary sortie generation rates and ISR availability (exercise metrics).
- P3: Increase maritime strike and counter-maritime escort. Integrate joint maritime fires (DDG/SSN simulated) as complementary effects; air missions provide cueing, confirmation, and time-sensitive engagement simulations.
- P1: Maintain suppression at a reduced but steady level; focus on nodes that most directly threaten HVAA routes and logistics corridors.
- P4: Increase non-kinetic sorties and RC-135 collection to degrade the adversary’s networked kill chain (data fusion, targeting coordination). Demonstrate operation with partial SATCOM loss by using AEHF for critical C2 and MUOS/UHF for tactical voice.

Sustainment posture:
- Shift from surge to sustainable generation; preserve a daily reserve margin for abort/refly and dynamic tasking.
- Plan for at least one “logistics disruption inject” every 48 hours (fuel/munitions/maintenance constraints). MAAP maintains flexibility via spares and cross-platform tasking.

PHASE 3 (Day 8+): Exploitation, Dynamic Targeting
Purpose: Demonstrate resilience and adaptation. Shift emphasis to P4 exploitation (kill chain disruption, deception, and rapid cycle assessment) while keeping protection (P5) and limited denial (P1–P3).

Key tasks:
- P4: Highest sortie share; run multiple short-notice, time-boxed missions inside comm windows to simulate rapid targeting, exploitation, and re-tasking under degraded SATCOM.
- Dynamic targeting: Use pre-briefed “if-then” triggers (e.g., OPIR/ISR cue + threat level) to execute on-call packages without requiring continuous connectivity.
- P5: Maintain DCA and escort; anticipate adversary “last-day surge” injects.
- P1–P3: Conduct limited re-attacks as needed to keep corridors open and prevent adversary endgame maritime/air surge.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
4. SPACE SUPPORT REQUIREMENTS
--------------------------------------------------------------------
4.1 PNT / GPS Coverage and “Precision Engagement Windows”
Baseline: GPS constellation is operational; however MDIX injects include localized PNT degradation and intermittent timing errors. For planning simplicity, MAAP defines daily “precision windows” when expected PNT quality and timing dissemination are adequate for precision-simulated engagements and synchronized package timing.

Precision Engagement Windows (daily, exercise-controlled; subject to EXCON adjustment):
- Window W1: 0300Z–0500Z (primary suppression/strike window)
- Window W2: 1530Z–1730Z (secondary strike/counterair window)

Outside W1/W2:
- Assume degraded PNT in at least one operating sector. Mitigations: inertial navigation emphasis, timing checks at takeoff, brevity/time-based routing, and increased reliance on preplanned control measures.

Priority use of PNT quality:
- Highest: P1 suppression corridors, P2 counterair timing, P3 time-sensitive maritime simulations.
- Moderate: P5 CAP (can accept degraded PNT with procedural control).
- Variable: P4 (often non-kinetic; timing still important for synchronized effects).

4.2 SATCOM Allocation by Mission Type (Bandwidth and Resilience Plan)
Available wideband SATCOM includes WGS (with some satellites degraded) and alternate transport. Protected SATCOM includes AEHF/Milstar; tactical SATCOM includes MUOS.

Allocation rules (planned; adjusted by JICO/Space Cell daily):
- AEHF/Milstar (Protected/EHF): reserved for mission-critical C2, ATO/ACO updates to airborne C2 nodes, and critical reporting when contested.
  • Primary users: “SENTRY” (AWACS), package leads for P1/P2 during W1/W2, and any long-range coordination messages (exercise-simulated “bomber-like” coordination will use EHF even if no bombers are flown).
- MUOS (UHF tactical SATCOM): primary for fighter tactical voice beyond LOS and procedural updates to CAPs, escorts, and recovery coordination.
  • Primary users: P5 DCA CAPs, P3 maritime packages, CSAR alert coordination.
- WGS/TDRS/Commercial-like wideband (best effort): used for bulk ISR relay, mission data updates pre-push, and non-time-critical reporting; expect intermittent degradation.
  • Primary users: RC-135 data movement when available; post-mission products.

Degraded SATCOM posture:
- Assume at least one wideband path is unreliable each day. All mission packages will carry a minimum essential information set (MEIS) printed/loaded preflight to execute without updates for up to 6 hours.

4.3 ISR/OPIR Schedule for Detection and Warning
OPIR (SBIRS GEO/HEO and SDA tracking) provides continuous strategic warning; MDIX injects simulate intermittent latency to tactical users. MAAP integrates ISR collection and dissemination via time windows:

- OPIR-driven warning cues (continuous): used to trigger threat condition changes (GREEN/AMBER/RED) in ATO execution. Primary consumers: AOC, IAMD cell, “SENTRY,” and P5 CAP controllers.
- Space-based SIGINT/ISR windows (notional): leveraged for P3 maritime cueing and P1 emitter mapping. Expected best collection periods (daily): 0200Z–0600Z and 1400Z–1800Z.
- RC-135V on-station windows (planned daily):
  • Sortie 1: 0100Z–0700Z (supports W1 and post-window assessment)
  • Sortie 2: 0700Z–1300Z (threat warning, target development)
  • Sortie 3: 1300Z–1900Z (supports W2, maritime cueing)
  • Sortie 4: 1900Z–0100Z (night threat warning, P4 characterization)

ISR reporting priorities:
1) Immediate threat to HVAA and hubs (P5)
2) P1 IADS status and corridor viability
3) P2 air generation indicators
4) P3 maritime cueing
5) P4 network characterization (unless Phase 3)

--------------------------------------------------------------------
5. FLOW PLAN
--------------------------------------------------------------------
5.1 Airborne C2 (AWACS) Coverage Rotation
Objective: Provide continuous airborne early warning and procedural control support, with redundancy for comm degradation.

Planned “SENTRY” orbits (generic; detailed control measures in ACO):
- Orbit NORTH: supports Japan main-island approaches and transit corridors
- Orbit SOUTH: supports Okinawa/Philippine Sea approaches and carrier operating area

Rotation (daily):
- 0000Z–0600Z: SENTRY-1 on-station (SOUTH), SENTRY-2 on-call (ground/alert)
- 0600Z–1200Z: SENTRY-2 on-station (NORTH), SENTRY-1 recovery
- 1200Z–1800Z: SENTRY-3 on-station (SOUTH), SENTRY-2 recovery
- 1800Z–2400Z: SENTRY-4 on-station (NORTH), SENTRY-3 recovery

Minimum requirement: 3 of 4 scheduled lines must execute daily to meet P5 and deconfliction objectives. If an AWACS line cancels, transition to procedural control: preplanned CAP timing gates and radar coverage from surface units (exercise-simulated integration).

5.2 Tanker Tracks and Sortie Flow (per 6-hour period)
Tanker support is simulated but scheduled to drive realistic flow, timing, and deconfliction. Tracks are generic and deconflicted from civil lanes per ACO.

Tanker tracks (generic):
- TRK-ALPHA: supports Kadena-based packages (east/west transit)
- TRK-BRAVO: supports Misawa-based packages (north sector)
- TRK-CHARLIE: supports carrier air wing push (Philippine Sea sector)

Daily tanker lines (baseline; adjust with weather and threat):
- 0000Z–0600Z: 4 tanker sorties total (2x ALPHA, 1x BRAVO, 1x CHARLIE)
- 0600Z–1200Z: 3 tanker sorties total (1x ALPHA, 1x BRAVO, 1x CHARLIE)
- 1200Z–1800Z: 4 tanker sorties total (2x ALPHA, 0–1x BRAVO, 1–2x CHARLIE depending on P3)
- 1800Z–2400Z: 3 tanker sorties total (1x ALPHA, 1x BRAVO, 1x CHARLIE)

Sortie flow construct (per 6-hour block; fighters only, excluding CAP persistence counted within block)
Block A (0000Z–0600Z): “Set conditions”
- Launch emphasis: DCA handover flights + P1 staging + RC-135 Sortie 1
- Planned fighter launches: 20–26 (mix of P5 CAP refresh and P1 pre-window presence)

Block B (0600Z–1200Z): “W1 exploitation and recovery”
- Launch emphasis: P1 window execution, limited P2, CAP continuity
- Planned fighter launches: 24–30 (highest density during Days 1–3)
- Recovery emphasis: rapid turn where logistics allow; otherwise staggered to preserve maintenance

Block C (1200Z–1800Z): “W2 build”
- Launch emphasis: P2 and P3 build-up, ISR cueing, CAP refresh
- Planned fighter launches: 22–28 (Days 4–7 will skew toward P2/P3)

Block D (1800Z–2400Z): “W2 execution and reset”
- Launch emphasis: W2 execution, night CAP, RC-135 Sortie 4
- Planned fighter launches: 18–24 (lower density to accommodate resets and degraded comm procedures)

Daily CAP continuity requirement (P5):
- Maintain at least two CAP lines continuously (one hub defense, one maritime/LOC). Each CAP line requires 4–6 sorties per 24 hours depending on duration. MAAP funds this via P5 allocation and reserves.

5.3 Package Timing and Degraded Comms Control
- All major strikes/suppression missions are anchored to W1/W2 precision windows.
- If SATCOM/datalink drops, package lead executes pre-briefed timing gates:
  • Gate 1: push time (no earlier than planned)
  • Gate 2: abort time (if separation/deconfliction cannot be confirmed)
  • Gate 3: recovery stack time (procedural)
- Dynamic retasking is restricted to “retask windows” when AEHF connectivity is expected:
  • Retask Window R1: 0430Z–0500Z
  • Retask Window R2: 1630Z–1700Z
Outside R1/R2, only safety-of-flight and immediate threat warnings will be transmitted.

6. ASSESSMENT CRITERIA (MEASURES OF EFFECTIVENESS)
--------------------------------------------------------------------
Assessment is effects-based and tied to each JIPTL priority. The AOC Strategy/Combat Assessment teams will compile daily metrics to inform the next ATO cycle.

PRIORITY 1 (P1) — A2/AD Node Cluster

MOE-P1.3 Survivability: No simulated loss of HVAA attributable to unmitigated IADS corridors (tracked via EXCON adjudication).
